summary: mypy rejects a raise_for_status call in Requester.getStream because the guard preceding it does not narrow the value to a type that has that method.
root_cause: __requestEncode is annotated to return Tuple[int, Dict[str, Any], Union[str, object]], so its third result is statically just object. The guard 'isinstance(output, RequestsResponse) or hasattr(output, "iter_content")' narrows to RequestsResponse only on its left branch; the hasattr branch contributes a type known solely to have iter_content, and mypy joins the two back to object. RequestsResponse does define raise_for_status, so the wrapper is not at fault: the disjunctive guard discards the isinstance narrowing. This is why iter_content on the following line type-checks while raise_for_status does not, and why only one error is reported.
recommended_action: Narrow the value with a single isinstance check against RequestsResponse before calling raise_for_status, or tighten __requestEncode's return annotation so the third element is not typed as bare object.
